apiContracts: Opening an unlocked chapter records reading history but never creates or changes a bookmark.
POST /api/bookmark saves only the exact chapter explicitly selected by the authenticated reader.
DELETE /api/bookmark removes only the selected (user_id, novel_id, chapter_number) row where user_id is derived from the authenticated session.
Both write methods use parseReaderProgressTarget and reject malformed, fractional, zero, negative or unsafe identifiers.
Guest bookmarks remain local to the browser and can be explicitly toggled off.

migrationPlan.canonicalEntityReuse: Reuses the existing bookmarks table and owner-scoped uniqueness; no new persistent entity.
migrationPlan.backwardCompatibility: Existing bookmarks remain intact. Removing a bookmark is an explicit DELETE and opening chapters no longer overwrites the user's saved bookmark.
migrationPlan.rollbackOrForwardRepair: Code-only rollback; no database migration or data rewrite is needed.

uiLifecycle.clientBootBehavior: The reader bookmark control reflects saved state, exposes aria-pressed, and toggles only from an explicit click.

privacySecurity.authentication: Bookmark writes require the existing authenticated session; guests use browser-local state only.
privacySecurity.authorization: The Worker derives the bookmark owner from session u.id.
privacySecurity.ownerScoping: DELETE predicates include user_id=u.id, novel_id and chapter_number. No client-supplied owner ID is accepted.
privacySecurity.csrf: Existing same-origin write-route policy remains in force.
privacySecurity.rateAndSizeLimits: Two positive safe-integer identifiers; bounded JSON payload.
privacySecurity.rightsAndPrivacy: Bookmark removal remains available for a user's own saved row even if the underlying story later becomes unpublished.

integration: Worker DELETE handler and browser source/served bundle parity assertions
isolation: Account A cannot remove account B's bookmark; DELETE is constrained to the exact chapter tuple.

stagingSteps: Run all exact-head architecture, source, route, schema, migration and Graphify workflows.
Verify chapter visits do not mutate bookmarks.
Verify explicit save/remove behavior for authenticated and guest readers.

rollback.codeRollback: Revert the reader handler and DELETE endpoint together; existing bookmark rows remain unchanged.
monitoringSignals: bookmark list and reader button state parity

collisionReview.duplicateRoutes: No new resource path; adds DELETE to the existing singular /api/bookmark resource.
collisionReview.sharedSurfaceOwners: Reader owns bookmark behavior; platform kernel owns Worker routing; experience shell owns the browser bundle; architecture inventories and tests are updated.

changeSummary: Stops silently bookmarking every opened chapter and makes bookmark creation/removal an explicit, accessible, owner-scoped reader action.
acceptanceCriteria: Opening a chapter never writes to bookmarks.
The explicit reader control toggles authenticated bookmarks through POST/DELETE.
Guest bookmarks can be saved and removed locally.
DELETE cannot affect another user's bookmark.
Invalid IDs are rejected before deletion.
The versioned browser bundle exactly matches public/app.js.
No migration or production data mutation is required.
